html:
Southern Cameroons was the southern part of British Cameroons, a strip of the former German Kamerun along the Nigerian border, ruled by Britain from 1922 to 1961. The map shows it in its 1945 snapshot.

After World War I the League of Nations gave most of Kamerun to France as French Cameroun and a smaller western part to Britain. Britain ran its share as part of Nigeria, and from 1946 it was a United Nations trust territory. The old German plantations around Mount Cameroon remained the main business.

In a plebiscite in 1961, the voters of Southern Cameroons chose to join the newly independent Republic of Cameroon, while Northern Cameroons joined Nigeria. English-speaking Southern Cameroonians later felt sidelined in a French-speaking state, a grievance that erupted in the Anglophone Crisis from 2016.
